name: Contemplating the Lord in his manifestations (vibhūti)
method_summary: Think of the Lord continually (paricintayan) by way of the things in which he is pre-eminently manifest — the chief member of each class (10.17–39) — and understand whatever being has glory, splendour or vigour as sprung from a portion of his splendour (10.41). The list is given 'by the chief ones' and only by way of indication, since his manifestations are endless (10.19, 10.40).
signs_of_progress: One who knows this vibhūti and yoga of his in truth is joined with unwavering yoga (10.7).
notes: Named here after Arjuna's question 'in which things are you to be thought of by me?' (10.17); the text gives no further procedure.

name: Enlightening one another and speaking of the Lord (bodhayantaḥ parasparam kathayantaś ca mām)
method_summary: With citta on the Lord and prāṇa given to him, devotees enlighten one another and always speak of him, and are content and delight (10.9); to those ever joined who so worship with love he gives buddhiyoga (10.10).
signs_of_progress: Contentment and delight (tuṣyanti ca ramanti ca, 10.9); the gift of buddhiyoga (10.10).

name: Fixing manas and buddhi on the Lord
method_summary: Fix (āveśya) manas on the Lord and worship him, ever joined, with supreme faith (12.2); place manas in him alone and let buddhi enter him (12.8); the devotee dear to him has manas and buddhi offered to him (12.14).
stage: the first and highest step of the conditional sequence of 12.8–11
signs_of_progress: Held to be 'the most joined' (12.2); 'you will dwell in me alone thereafter' (12.8).
notes: Cf. 8.7 (mayy arpitamanobuddhiḥ). The next step (12.9) is for one who cannot fix citta steadily in him.

name: The yoga of practice (abhyāsa-yoga)
method_summary: For one unable to fix citta steadily on the Lord: seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (12.9). Chapter 12 does not describe the practice further; elsewhere the text uses abhyāsa for bringing the wandering mind back again and again (6.26, 6.35) and speaks of a 'yoga of practice' with the mind not straying to anything else (8.8).
stage: second step of 12.8–11 (for one unable to fix citta steadily)
prerequisites: The text addresses it to one not able to fix citta steadily on the Lord (12.9).
notes: 12.12 ranks knowledge above practice. Related: prc:abhyasa-vairagya (practice with dispassion, 6.35), which 12.9 does not mention.

name: Doing the Lord's work (mat-karma)
method_summary: If unable even in practice, be intent on work for the Lord (matkarmaparama); even doing actions for his sake one attains perfection (12.10). 'One who does my work (matkarmakṛt), holds me highest, is devoted to me, free from attachment and without enmity toward any being comes to me' (11.55).
signs_of_progress: Attainment of perfection (siddhi, 12.10); coming to the Lord (11.55).

name: Relinquishing the fruit of all actions
method_summary: If unable to do even the Lord's work: resorting to his yoga, self-restrained, relinquish the fruit of all actions (12.11). It is then ranked above meditation (which is above knowledge, which is above practice), and peace follows relinquishment immediately (12.12).
stage: fourth step of 12.8–11; ranked highest in 12.12
notes: The commentators divide on how the ranking of 12.12 relates to 12.11's placing of relinquishment as the step for the least able.

name: Resigning all actions to the Lord (mayi sarvāṇi karmāṇi saṃnyasya)
method_summary: Those who renounce all actions in the Lord, intent on him, and worship him meditating with yoga directed to nothing else (12.6) — for them, whose cetas has entered him, he becomes before long the deliverer from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).
signs_of_progress: Swift deliverance by the Lord from the ocean of death and saṃsāra (12.7).

name: Worship of the imperishable unmanifest (akṣara-upāsanā)
method_summary: Worship (paryupāsate) of the imperishable — indefinable, unmanifest, all-pervading, unthinkable, unchanging, immovable, fixed — having restrained the whole group of senses, even-minded everywhere, delighting in the welfare of all beings; those who so worship also reach the Lord (12.3–4).
prerequisites: Restraint of all the senses; evenness of understanding everywhere; delight in the welfare of all beings (12.4).

warnings.text: The hardship is greater for those whose cetas is attached to the unmanifest; for the unmanifest goal is reached with pain by the embodied (12.5).

notes: The referent of 'the imperishable' is disputed by the commentators (see dsp:bhagavad-gita-manifest-or-unmanifest-worship).

name: Mantra repetition (japa)
method_summary: 'Of sacrifices I am the sacrifice of recitation (japa-yajña); of utterances, the single syllable' (10.25).

name: Obeisance and adoration (vandana)
method_summary: Arjuna bows his head to the Lord with joined palms (11.14); does homage trembling and bowing low (11.35); offers homage a thousand times, in front, behind and on every side (11.39–40); and, bowing and prostrating his body, seeks the Lord's grace and forgiveness (11.44).
